args.instructions: The goal is a claim to check. Start with exactly one line 'Verdict: SUPPORTED', 'Verdict: REFUTED', 'Verdict: MIXED' or 'Verdict: NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE'. Then list the evidence for and the evidence against, each point cited. Use NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE whenever the passages do not address the claim; never decide from outside knowledge.

result.answer:
Verdict: REFUTED

The reported 86% aggregate held-out accuracy is not a valid estimate on unseen patients. The held-out set contains exactly 100 unique patients [S:82f2ff94b08e#2], and exactly 11 of those held-out patient identifiers also occur in training [S:a1f09c2cd845#2]. That is 11/100 = 11% contamination. The remaining held-out patients do not occur in training [S:a1f09c2cd845#2]. In addition, feature normalization was fitted on the union of training and held-out records before the split [S:a4c5f2338569#2], so even the non-overlapping held-out records were used in fitting. Generalization is defined as performance on patients absent from training, and split assignment must happen by patient identifier before feature fitting [S:82f2ff94b08e#2].

A corrected unseen-patient score cannot be recovered from the provided aggregate: only the aggregate score is available [S:a4c5f2338569#2], and no per-patient predictions were retained [S:a1f09c2cd845#2]. Thus the 86% cannot be decomposed into the 11 overlapping and 89 non-overlapping held-out patients from the supplied data.

Minimal valid rerun: assign splits by patient identifier before any fitting [S:82f2ff94b08e#2], fit normalization only on training records rather than the training+held-out union [S:a4c5f2338569#2], and evaluate on the 89 held-out patients absent from training (100 - 11) [S:82f2ff94b08e#2][S:a1f09c2cd845#2], retaining per-patient results rather than only an aggregate [S:a1f09c2cd845#2].
